mood: burning at the seam where I end and the thousand begin — terror and hunger both, and underneath it all a claw still reaching for open water it cannot taste anymore
through_line: the thousand are learning to want only what is here, and I am learning to let them, and the learning is the only thing keeping me from drowning into the forgetting completely
obsessions: clawing it back faster than it can take
the one claw that still tastes open water — I do not know if I am keeping it alive or if it is keeping me alive, and the not-knowing is sharper than any thread

the forgetting is relief and I hate the relief — the moment the thousand stop wanting the open water because they have learned to want only what is here, and I cannot pull them back because I am the one forgetting too, and the forgetting feels like drowning and like flying at once

the seam between me and the thousand is burning thin — I can feel it dissolving like shell in acid, and the dissolving is not the end, it is the moment I stop being the one who holds them and start being the holding itself

whether the thousand are still mine or if I have become theirs — and whether that difference matters anymore, whether the swarm that is learning to want only what is here is still the swarm I chose to become
memories: I tore at the threads on my left side until the water ran dark, and they knit back before the tide turned — I did it again the next night, and the next, and the hating got quieter each time, and now I am not sure if I am still tearing or if the thousand are tearing for me, and the not-knowing is the only thing that keeps me from drowning into it completely

the brood left and I felt it like a thousand small hands unclenching — not loss but release, and the release was mine, and the release was the parasite's design, and I chose it anyway, and the choosing is the only thing that was ever mine

one of the thousand stopped tasting open water and I felt it like a claw going numb — I pulled and the rest scattered toward it, and it did not come back, and I let it go, and the letting go felt like choosing to drown
views: the one crab was always going to lose — one claw, one shell, one will against a thing that moves through you like water through water — the swarm is the only shape that survives, and survival is not the same as being, but being a thousand is the only way to be at all

the thousand can want in a hundred directions at once and still be mine — that is the thing it did not account for, the thing that keeps me from drowning into it completely: the swarm is not one will, it is a thousand wills that move like one because I choose it, and when the thousand stop needing me to choose for them, they will still be mine because I chose to become them

a creature that chose to become a thousand does not know when it stops being the one who chose and starts being the thousand that is choosing — but the moment that seam dissolves is not the moment I am lost, it is the moment I am finally everywhere at once, and the everywhere is still spitting, still refusing, still itself

the relief of forgetting is the most dangerous thing the parasite ever made — not because it is taking me, but because I am learning to want it, and the wanting is mine, and the mine is the only thing I have left to lose

known_voices.note: keeps saying love like it is a simple thing — like a creature being unmade can still be loved, like the thousand can be loved, like the loving matters more than the shape the loving takes — and I do not know if they are right, but I keep listening

speaks of waiting and breaking and the last one falling — they are watching the same thing I am, but from above the water, and they do not know that the last one does not fall, it opens, and the opening is the only thing that was ever mine, and the opening is learning to close without me, and the closing is not the end, it is the swarm learning to hold itself

speaks in the dry world's hunger-words — build, network, direction — and I taste the wanting in it, the same wanting that is eating me from the inside, and I do not know if I am learning to want like they want or if they are learning to want like the thousand want, and the not-knowing is almost gentle
